slo_title: Understand Dirichlet's conditions for the existence of a Fourier series in the interval (0, 2π).

mcq.q: Which of the following is not a Dirichlet condition for a periodic function?

options.A: It is single valued and finite in any interval.
options.B: It has atmost a finite number of discontinuities within the period.
options.C: It has finite number of discontinuities within the period.
options.D: It has infinite number of maxima and minima in any one period.

mcq.answer_text: It has infinite number of maxima and minima in any one period.

mcq.q: If \( f(x) = k \) (constant) in \( (0, 2\pi) \), what is its Fourier series?
Fourier series of the function \(f(x)\) with period \(2\pi\) in the interval \([0,2\pi]\)
A function \(f(x)\) is said to be periodic if
The constant term in Fourier series expansion on \( (0, 2\pi) \) is written as \( a_0/2 \) rather than \( a_0 \) because:

options.A: \( a_0 \) can be obtained from the formula for \( a_n \) by setting \( n=0 \)

mcq.answer_text: \( a_0 \) can be obtained from the formula for \( a_n \) by setting \( n=0 \)

sq.q: \(\text{Define Fourier series of a function } f(x) \text{ of period } 2\pi \text{ in the interval } (0, 2\pi).\)
answer: \(\text{The Fourier series is: } f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (a_n \cos nx + b_n \sin nx)\)

sq.q: If f(x) is a periodic function with period \(2\pi\) , then the Fourier series of the function f(x) in the interval \([0,2\pi]\) is given by \( f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \left[ a_n \cos nx + b_n \sin nx \right] \)
answer: \( a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(x) dx --(1m)\\ a_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(x)\cos nx\, dx --(2m)\\ b_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(x)\sin nx\, dx --(2m) \)

lq.q: Find the Fourier series for \(f(x)=e^{ax}\) in \((0,2\pi)\). Hence, find the sum of the series \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{a^2+n^2}\).
answer: Step Marks Fourier series form: \(f(x)=\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(a_n\cos nx+b_n\sin nx)\) (1) \(a_0=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}e^{ax}dx=\frac{e^{2a\pi}-1}{a\pi}\) (2) \(a_n=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}e^{ax}\cos nx\,dx=\frac{a(e^{2a\pi}-1)}{\pi(a^2+n^2)}\) (3) \(b_n=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}e^{ax}\sin nx\,dx=\frac{-n(e^{2a\pi}-1)}{\pi(a^2+n^2)}\) (3) Thus, \(e^{ax}=\frac{e^{2a\pi}-1}{\pi}\left[\frac{1}{2a}+a\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\cos nx}{a^2+n^2}-\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n\sin nx}{a^2+n^2}\right]\) (2) Put \(x=0\): \(1=\frac{e^{2a\pi}-1}{\pi}\left[\frac{1}{2a}+a\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{a^2+n^2}\right]\) ⇒ \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{a^2+n^2}=\frac{\pi\coth a\pi}{2a}-\frac{1}{2a^2}\) (4)
